sentences.text: Markus Krebber, born 16 February 1973 in Kleve, has been chief executive officer of RWE AG, the Essen-based energy group, since 1 May 2021.
He trained as a bank clerk at Deutsche Bank, studied economics in Duisburg and Pennsylvania, then worked as a consultant at McKinsey while completing a doctorate at Humboldt University in Berlin.

sentences.text: From 2005 to 2012 he held several leadership roles at Commerzbank in Frankfurt, latterly as divisional board member and head of group finance.

He joined RWE in November 2012 as managing director and chief financial officer of RWE Supply & Trading, later leading that unit, and was chief financial officer of RWE AG from October 2016 until April 2021, succeeding Rolf Martin Schmitz as CEO.

mgmt_bio.text: Markus Krebber, born 16 February 1973 in Kleve, has been chief executive officer of RWE AG, the Essen-based energy group, since 1 May 2021. From 2005 to 2012 he held several leadership roles at Commerzbank in Frankfurt, latterly as divisional board member and head of group finance. In July 2025 the supervisory board extended his contract early by five years, until the end of June 2031.

citations.title: RWE delivers strong financial performance in 2025 and sets course for exceptional earnings growth until 2031

sentences.quote: Between 2026 and 2031, RWE plans to make a total of EUR 35 billion in net investments to expand its portfolio, thereby increasing its renewable, battery storage and flexible generation capacity by 25 gigawatts (GW) to around 65 GW.
sentences.text: RWE plans net investments of 35 billion euros between 2026 and 2031, lifting renewable, battery storage and flexible generation capacity by 25 gigawatts to about 65 gigawatts.
Management expects the programme to yield average returns above 8.5 percent and adjusted earnings per share to rise from 2.48 euros to about 4.40 euros by 2031.
Shareholder returns rest on a dividend target growing 10 percent a year, with 1.32 euros per share envisaged for fiscal 2026, alongside a 1.5 billion euro share buyback completed in June 2026.
Strong first-half 2026 results, with adjusted EBITDA up 44 percent to 3.0 billion euros, led RWE to raise its 2026 guidance to 5.75 to 6.35 billion euros.
